POST with revision greater than current accepted. CLI `mosslight inspect missing.json` exit 1. render_map(layer='shade') with shade_cloth shows base shade. render_history with history days [5,6,20] spaced evenly.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign fixes: (1) runtime.execution_version ignored the campaign's recorded release and always ran conservation-2, so classic-1 campaigns used the wrong rain-barrel ecology; now uses definition["runtime"]["id"]; (2) publish accepted stale results: WHERE (generation = ? OR owner != ?) let a worker whose lease was reclaimed overwrite progress – now requires generation AND owner match; (3) publish committed branch progress before writing its checkpoint/report in a second transaction – a crash between left progress without checkpoint/report; now one transaction; (4) fork re-applied events at the checkpoint offset although that care is already part of the checkpoint garden (offset <= → <); (5) compact computed protected lineage checkpoints but never used them, deleting fork origins so provenance failed.

provisional_claims.summary: History fixes: (1) replay checkpoint cache keyed only on the LAST event (events[-1:]) so a corrected/rebased history sharing a final event reused a stale cached garden – now keyed on the full prefix; (2) resolved references used the author's recorded local number (bindings) instead of the logical object's current ID, so after a correction renumbered objects later edits hit the wrong/unrelated object; (3) correct() canonicalized numeric IDs in replacements against the FINAL original garden instead of the garden at that point in the revised history; (4) cherry-pick deduplicated by command content digest, so independently authored identical actions were dropped – identity is now the event ID; (5) rebase order check ignored the local branch's authored order (only target), so contradictory shared orders weren't reported; (6) rebase used the parent's CURRENT head as merge base instead of the fork's recorded base_revision, treating parent's later events as base and losing/garbling changes.

provisional_claims.summary: courier.py (field courier CRDT) fixes: (1) precedes() iterated the wrong clock's keys, so an event was treated as superseded by any event whose context lacked its writer -> concurrent edits from other writers were silently dropped; (2) _covered() used the max over ALL records' contexts, so sharing/compacting one observation implied the recipient had seen other observations' edits (docs forbid) — now per-record context; (3) project() kept contexts of unselected records, so merging a selection into a full notebook discarded observations it did not include; (4) merge only compared the record of a reused dot — conflicting reuse (different value/field) now rejected; (5) merged packet kept the left counter even when the right copy held newer events by that writer, so continuing emitted duplicate dots; (6) observations() casefolded values, merging distinct texts differing in case (docs: text retains exact case); (7) concurrent edit+deletion hid the observation (docs: keep visible); (8) acknowledged() used max instead of min over named devices; (9) put() stored caller-owned values by reference; recover() on non-string now a clear ValueError.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble fixes: (1) ensemble_compute.evaluate returned the cached computation's ORIGIN identity on a cache hit, so two sources with equal saves (or reuse across trials) collapsed into one comparison member – identity is now always the requested replicate/treatment; (2) ensemble_reports.summarize paired controls with trials by zip(controls.values(), ...) order instead of by replicate, so treatments were compared with another garden's control whenever a control failed/was excluded or ordering differed; (3) EnsembleStore.publish validated only the node's PREVIOUS reads (empty for first computations) against current inputs, so a result computed from pre-edit inputs could be published for a newer revision – now validates the reads actually used; (4) report() recomputed the result from CURRENT outcomes instead of returning the archived envelope, so published reports for earlier revisions changed after later edits.

Finish revision 0, edit plan:water, work → report(revision=0) shows revision-1 numbers. prepare ticket, edit plan the node reads, publish → accepted with stale data.

provisional_claims.summary: save_merge.py: _logical_id ignored origin and base ids, so records independently created on both replicas with the same numeric id were treated as the same record (merged/conflicted instead of kept separate with fresh ids; docs: "Independently created records stay separate, even if the devices gave them the same number"). Now non-inherited ids are keyed by replica origin and reallocated. Also added a common-ancestor sanity check: a replica whose day or revision precedes the supplied original is rejected (seed/size match alone insufficient).

provisional_claims.summary: Study fixes: (1) later stages started every treatment job from the previous stage's CONTROL checkpoint (checkpoint(..., "control")), discarding the promoted treatment's earlier care/results – now each job continues its own treatment's checkpoint; (2) stage decisions were finalized as soon as ONE garden had complete control+treatments (before all trials finished/failed), so worker completion order decided promotion, and a stage with no eligible garden never recorded its failed decision – now waits for readiness()['terminal'], then records a failed decision when no source is eligible.

A study where every control fails stayed 'running' forever.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier fix: events recorded the packet's GLOBAL clock as their causal context, and checkpoint() stamped every record's context with the global clock. After merging a projection (whose clock covers unshared observations), a writer's later edit of another observation—or a checkpoint—claimed to have seen edits it never received, silently superseding/dropping them (docs: sharing one observation does not imply the recipient has seen another observation's edits; compacting/selecting must preserve meaning). Contexts are now per-record (record_clock) in _emit and checkpoint.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier: event contexts and checkpoint contexts used the packet-wide clock, so after merging a projection (which carries the full clock) a device's later edit silently superseded concurrent edits to observations it never received, and checkpoint marked unseen records as covered (dropping them on later merge). Now contexts use per-record record_clock. Also campaigns: runtime.execution_version ignored the campaign's recorded release (always conservation-2).
